correctness.rationale: In the stated exactly-two-agent, two equally abundant chore-type model, r>1 crossed wrong-agent A and B chores permit a strict fractional Pareto improvement; absence of a cross is sufficient by strictly positive weighted-sum minimization. On either fPO branch, the binding EFX inequality is j≤t/2−(t−1)/(2r). The two branches contain binom(t,j) labeled allocations per j and overlap exactly once. At r=1, all allocations are fPO and EFX is exactly equal bundle cardinality. Integer floor crossing yields listed inclusive jump ratios; fixed r>1 binomial tail Stirling gives h2((r−1)/(2r)). Independently enumerated all 4^t labeled allocations for 1≤t≤5 at six exact rational r values, testing owner-by-owner EFX and crossed-case fPO, agreeing with formula in 30 parameter instances. Actual verify_chores.py read and checks more cases. Finite tests do not establish all real r or t.
